descriptionAdvanced.en: The Guabirá Sugar Mill (Ingenio Azucarero Guabirá) is the largest and most advanced agro-industrial complex in Bolivia, located in the city of Montero, Santa Cruz. Founded in 1956, it has grown from a state-led project into a successful cooperative owned by over 1,500 shareholders, including local sugarcane farmers. The mill is the nation's leader in the production of refined sugar and has recently pioneered the large-scale production of anhydrous ethanol for use as a biofuel. Guabirá's operation is central to the food security of Bolivia and is a major contributor to the country's exports. The facility is also recognized for its commitment to social responsibility and sustainable practices, holding several international certifications for its environmental management and labor standards.

en: Guabirá processes more than 3 million tons of sugarcane per year.
The mill produces roughly 30% of the total sugar consumed in the Bolivian domestic market.
It is the first company in Bolivia to receive the 'Triple Seal' certification for child labor-free production.
The facility also generates its own electricity using biomass from sugarcane bagasse.
